mainEntity.name: How much extra tile should I buy?

acceptedAnswer.text: Ten percent is the usual minimum for a straight layout. Add more for diagonal, herringbone or mosaic patterns, and for rooms with many corners or obstacles.

mainEntity.name: How much grout do I need?

acceptedAnswer.text: It depends on tile size, thickness and joint width. Small tiles and wide joints need much more grout than large tiles with narrow joints. This tool works from the joint volume and adds 25% for waste and uneven surfaces.

Sanded grout is normally used for joints of 1/8 inch and wider because it resists shrinking and cracking. Unsanded grout suits narrower joints and soft or polished stone that sand could scratch. Epoxy grout resists stains and chemicals.

mainEntity.name: What trowel notch should I use?

acceptedAnswer.text: Small tiles usually take a 1/4 in square notch, mid-size tiles a 1/4 × 3/8 in notch, and large-format tiles a 1/2 in square notch or larger. Always follow the mortar bag instructions and check for full coverage under the tile.
Thicker tile has deeper joints, so it takes more grout. The tile-and-joint size also changes how many tiles fit in an area.
